Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report states that when either endpoint of the bracket interval is a root (i.e., the function value at that endpoint is zero or within a small accuracy), the solver returns the function value yMin or yMax instead of the endpoint coordinate min or max.

Inspecting the code of BrentSolver.solve(f, min, max, initial), we see the following:
- At line 113, the function value yMin = f.value(min) is computed.
- At line 114, if |yMin| <= functionValueAccuracy (close enough to zero), the solver calls setResult(yMin, 0) and returns result.
- Similarly for yMax at lines 125-128, it calls setResult(yMax, 0) and returns result.

The setResult method in the parent class UnivariateRealSolverImpl.setResult(double newResult, int iterationCount) simply assigns this.result = newResult, i.e., it sets the solver's result to the function value, not to the input coordinate. Therefore, if yMin or yMax is close to zero, the solver returns the function value (which is zero-ish) rather than the coordinate min or max.

This is the cause of the bug as described: "returns yMin or yMax if min or max are roots, instead of min or max." The failure in the test shows that the solver is returning a value of ~0 instead of Math.PI, which is expected to be the root.

The root cause is the misuse of setResult with the function value as argument instead of the coordinate of the root. The code should store and return min or max when the endpoint is detected as the root, not the value yMin or yMax.

No other recent bug reports are directly relevant to this endpoint root detection issue.

This diagnosis explains the test failure and matches the bug report's description precisely.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
